events.context: Provides detailed explanation of Tarot elements: Fire (Wands), Water (Cups), Air (Swords), Earth (Pentacles), including domains, meanings, imbalances, and elemental dynamics in spreads. Offers to apply to specific spreads.
User describes struggle with capsule wardrobe, asks how many outfits (looks) a 'small cat-like beauty' (rare refined girl in Lixin university) needs per quarter.
AI uses common sense: 12-18 effective looks per quarter (8-10 daily rotations, 3-5 signature looks, 2-3 flexible). Emphasizes style consistency over quantity. Offers further help.
User asks to mathematically estimate the probability.
Sets conditions: 16,000 students, 68% female (~10,880). Layers: 3% top appearance (326), 30% top style (98), 15% aura (15). Adjusts to 2-3 perceived via visibility. Ties back to 12-18 looks.
Notes two campuses, so halve; mentions Parkinsons/Pareto law.
Refines: 20,000 students, 13,600 females. 0.1% 'cat-like' =13.6 total. Per campus: 5-7 objective, 2-4 perceived. Applies Pareto: 20% stylish, top 5% refined. Concludes 2-4 visible.
Asks for percentage, equates to 'yan zhi scores' (beauty ratings).
Maps to 10-point scale: 8.5-9 = cat-like (0.3-0.5%, 24-40 objective, 2-3 perceived). Distinguishes objective vs. subjective (style+aura). Ties to wardrobe.
Agrees 9+ empty in non-elite schools. Explains as social safety cap, anchors 8=Tang Yan, 9=Fan Bingbing. Cat-like=8-8.5.
Reiterates 9+ vacant, asks why scoring designed this way, suggests anchors like Fan Bingbing=9, Tang Yan=8.
Explains scoring as social language, not math: 9+ suspended for celebrities. Campus ceiling 8.5. Provides honest table.
Explains beauty as long-tail distribution, misfit to 1-10 linear scale causes high-end sparsity, mid dense. Examples of 6-rated variance.
Confirms: beauty long-tail, but public uses linear 1-10, compressing mid, sparsifying high-end.
